$comment: Configuration for scripts/figma/compare-ui.mjs and harvest-ui.mjs (Plan 217). `components` says how to render each Figma set in Storybook: the story, the element to measure, and how a Figma variant's properties become story args (`args`: Figma property to arg name; `values`: Figma value to arg value, where they differ) and interactions (`state`: hover and pressed are made by the harvester). `allow` lists differences the owner accepted, each with a reason; an entry that matches nothing fails the run.

allow.reason: Figma draws a fixed 240px frame; in code the input is w-full and takes its container (320px in the story). Width is layout, not look.
Code shows the placeholder attribute, which is not a text node; Figma draws a text layer so the placeholder can be edited and styled.
Both hug their content now (padding, gap and type match). The story card holds different copy than the Figma placeholder content, so its height differs.
Figma draws a fixed 240px frame; in code the textarea is w-full and takes its container (384px in the story). Width is layout, not look.
Code shows the placeholder attribute, which is not a text node; Figma draws a text layer so the placeholder can be edited and styled.
Figma draws a fixed 400px frame; in code the alert is w-full and takes its container.
Code positions the icon absolutely beside the text (no flex gap); Figma uses an auto-layout gap of alert.gap to place the icon, the result looks the same.
The story wraps the bar in a shrink-wrapped box, so w-full measures 0; Figma draws a 240px track.
Follows from the 0px width in the story: the radius is clamped to half the width. The token (4px) matches Figma.
The UI label is an inline element holding the story copy ("Email Address"); Figma draws the word Label. Width follows the copy.
An inline label measures its font content area (22px at md), not its line height; the text layer line height matches.
Figma gap 4 sits between the label and the optional required indicator, which is hidden here; the UI label is inline text.
Figma draws a fixed 200px trigger; in code the trigger is w-full and takes its container (320px in the story).
Figma draws a fixed 240px line; in code the separator is w-full.
The Separator story renders horizontally only, so the vertical variant is not rendered by this run and measures 0.
The story forces className w-48 h-4, so the size and variant axes are overridden; Figma draws the token sizes.
The story forces className w-48 h-4, so the size and variant axes are overridden; Figma draws the token sizes.
Follows from the story forcing w-48 h-4: the radius is clamped to half the 16px height. The Figma radius is the token.
The UI pulses; the measurement catches a frame mid-animation (0.86 to 0.88). Figma draws the resting 1.
Figma fills the avatar root with the fallback background; the UI root has avatar.background under a full-size fallback of the same size, so the visible result is the fallback color.
The story gives AvatarFallback no size, so its text stays at md (14px); the component scales it when size is passed (avatar.fallback font-size tokens), which is what Figma draws.
Same as font size: the story keeps the md fallback line height.
